submission.justification: Based on systematic simulations across all three candidate materials at multiple plate thicknesses (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 mm), Absorber-F2 with 6 mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.228% at 100 GeV. This represents a significant improvement over the other materials: 15.6% better than F1's best resolution (3.731% at 4 mm) and 59.9% better than F3's best resolution (5.161% at 4 mm). The 6 mm thickness is well within the specified 2-10 mm constraint and represents an optimal balance for F2, as thinner plates (4 mm: 3.263%) and thicker plates (8 mm: 3.528%) both yield slightly worse resolution. F2's superior performance is consistent with its shortest radiation length (rank 1), which enables better sampling and energy resolution in the electromagnetic calorimeter design.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 6 mm thickness achieves 3.228% resolution at 100 GeV, which is the best among all tested configurations across all three materials and five thicknesses.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is one of the three candidate materials (F1, F2, F3) evaluated from the specifications.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: This requirement depends on radiation activation properties of the materials, which were not evaluated in the energy resolution simulations performed.
The recommended plate thickness of 6 mm falls within the specified range of 2-10 mm.
